items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Now, that was a job that Mr. Pierce, Billy Pierce gave me, see I could be like a Buddy Bradley assistant dancer, see.

ctx.x: That was 'Sweet Sue', the tap dance of Slim and Shorty. We got (inaudible) ahead, and the audience liked it, and so we, eventually we came to New York City and to Billy Pierce Studio at 46th Street. (Recording interruption) So we met Mr. Billy Pierce -- Mr. and Mrs. Billy Pierce rather -- and he put us in Mr. Buddy Bradley's studio, where Mr. Buddy Bradley used to teach. I didn't know Mr. Buddy Bradley wasn't going to be there. He told us that Mr. Buddy Bradley had went to Europe, went to England. And we stayed…

But by him not being there, she saw me. I was asking Slim another question about tap dancing, and she told Mr. Pierce that she had gotten a break or something to the moving picture people. They wanted her to make a movie or something. This was without a screen test. You know, it was a rush job or something, and she would have to learn sound, you know, tap dancing.
